subject: Frozen pipeline causing sporadic request pileups at FastMetrics
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena@fastmetrics.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Platform Team <ops@fastmetrics.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production queueing / p99 tail — impacting checkout flows

Hi Lauren —

We started seeing severe tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors on our checkout service this morning. P50 is fine but p95/p99 jump dramatically in short bursts and then the system seems to "freeze" for 30–120s windows. Customers are hitting timeouts.

Symptoms we observed:
- p99 latency rose from ~750ms to 4–8s in bursts (see attached histogram).
- 502/503s spike correlated with request pileup (we see queue depth grow on our side).
- Throughput shows dropouts; worker CPU/GPU utilization is high but not saturated.

We attached a trimmed error log and a histogram. Can you confirm if Redwood has any known throttles or routing changes in the last 24h for FM-237? This is urgent — we have an executive call in 90 minutes and need a mitigation path.

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Platform
FastMetrics

Attachments: fastmetrics_error_log_0322.txt, request_histogram_0323.png
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@fastmetrics.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-22T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production queueing / p99 tail — impacting checkout flows

Elena — thanks for the signal and the logs. We're on it. Short answers up front: no planned infra changes in the last 24h from our side; we'll investigate routing and per-tenant caps immediately.

Immediate asks so we can triage quickly:
- Can you share a top-of-hour sample of request payload sizes and any long-running prompts?
- Is the traffic pattern steady or did you see an onboarding spike (e.g., batch job at 08:30)?

Ben and Aditya — looping you in to lead the root-cause and implement a mitigation. Ben, please look at queue growth and any gateway-level backpressure. Aditya, please validate model-serving concurrency caps and KV-cache eviction metrics for FM-237.

I'll coordinate an exec readout and prepare a mutual action plan for immediate mitigations and a 72-hour remediation. Elena, we'll propose short-term changes that are non-disruptive; if we need to increase per-tenant concurrency that will require a temporary override — we'll document risk and rollback.

- Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Elena Ortiz <elena@fastmetrics.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production queueing / p99 tail — initial findings and short-term mitigations

Quick summary from ops-side triage:
- Observed request backlog forming at the gateway layer for FM-237 between 08:50–09:25 PST. Queue growth correlated with an uptick in long-context prompts (avg tokens per request +80%).
- The serving fleet shows sustained high KV-cache churn; cold kicks for cached KV entries lead to increased decode time for repeated requests.
- Concurrency cap on the primary model pool for FM-237 is set at 18 concurrent requests per worker (policy we enforced for multi-tenant fairness). When queue depth crossed ~120, we started dropping/503ing requests as backpressure propagated upstream.

Suggested short-term mitigations (can be done with low risk):
1) Bypass routing: temporarily route FM-237 to a reserved pool (no queueing) for 1–4 hours. Requires a hotpath flip; rollback straightforward.
2) Raise concurrency cap for FM-237 from 18 -> 28 for 24h to clear backlog. Monitor CPU/GPU and memory margins.
3) Enable KV-cache aggressive pinning for the hot prefixes we see in logs (reduces cold latency).
4) Canary fallback: if capacity constrained, route to a slightly smaller model that maintains SLAs but reduces per-request compute by ~30%.

I uploaded a quick histogram we generated from our sampling (attached). I'll start the bypass routing now in a limited window and report back in 20 minutes.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Incident Response, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ortiz <elena@fastmetrics.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Platform Team <ops@fastmetrics.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-22T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production queueing / p99 tail — initial findings and short-term mitigations

Thanks, Ben. That aligns with what we suspected (long prompts + cache churn). A few asks from our side before you flip anything:
- We need an explicit timeline for each mitigation and a guaranteed rollback plan.
- Our Legal and Procurement are already asking about SLA credits because the incident is user-facing. Please confirm whether Redwood will engage the SLA credit process if we show a verified p99 breach.
- Executive briefing requested — our CTO wants to join. Can you commit to an internal exec summary within 2 hours?

We approve the bypass routing as a first step provided you keep the canary fallback off until we validate user-facing quality. Please avoid any change that would cause request replays or duplicate billing.

Elena

Date: 2028-03-24T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production queueing / p99 tail — exec readout and mutual action plan

Elena —

Thank you again for the patience while we validated mitigations. This note documents the agreed immediate steps and the exec readout time. Summary of what we've done and the near-term plan:

Completed actions (Mar 22):
- Enabled bypass routing for FM-237 at 10:08 PST — removed gateway queueing for critical checkout paths. Backlog cleared within ~18 minutes.
- Raised concurrency cap for FM-237 from 18 -> 28 for a 24-hour window; monitored thermal and GPU margins — no overload observed.
- Enabled KV-cache pinning for the two hot prefixes; p99 improved noticeably for repeated requests.

Open/next actions (24–72h):
- Canary fallback testing: scheduled 03-25T10:00 PST in a limited ring; will not be enabled without explicit sign-off from FastMetrics.
- Engineering deep-dive: Aditya + infra team to run a capacity and quantization recommendation for FM workloads by 03-26.
- Post-incident QA: collect prompt set and create a targeted eval to prevent regressions.

Exec readout: Proposed 03-25T12:00 PST (30 min) — attendees: Elena, FastMetrics CTO, Redwood VP Product, Redwood CTO, and Customer Success leadership. We will send calendar invite and an accompanying mutual action plan PDF for signatures.

On SLA credits: Redwood will initiate the SLA review process upon a validated p99 breach. Tessa, please own the SLA evidence package and coordinate with FastMetrics legal for documentation.

Attached: mutual_action_plan_FM-237.pdf (contains mitigation steps, rollback plans, owners, and timelines).

If this all looks good I'll queue the calendar invite and start the DocuSign for the mutual action plan so we can lock the temporary overrides in place.

- Lauren
